text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make code easier to read, understand, and maintain. For example, you might rename unclear variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or remove repeated code. Refactoring does not add new features or fix bugs; the program should behave exactly the same after the changes. Regular refactoring helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when code is written quickly without attention to quality. Although it takes time, refactoring saves effort in the future and keeps a project healthy.
